messages:
Elaine Chen: FYI ArgosHealth is seeing p99 spikes (dedicated pool 'pool-east-2') since 08:37Z. They’re hitting SLA thresholds and raised this with support. Who can own a short-term mitigation + comms?
Mike Patel: on it. tagging @Ravi and @Sara — need owners for routing + pool scaling.
Ravi Kumar: I’ll take routing. Quick check shows queue_depth x4 and KV cache miss rate up. Possible kernel churn on the model variant they use. Pulling logs now.
incident-bot: INCIDENT-1234 created: ArgosHealth p99 latency spike (pool-east-2) — severity P1 — responders paged.
Sara Gomez: We can spin extra dedicated nodes in pool-east-2 but warm-up is ~6m. Immediate option: route traffic to smaller model variant open-7b-quant as a fallback to reduce latency. That requires a routing rule change.
Linda Park: ArgosHealth legal flagged this — they want a concrete workaround now and an ETA. Please confirm who is committing to the fallback + timeline.
Ravi Kumar: I can patch the routing policy now — will apply canary that shifts 70% to open-7b-quant while nodes scale. Need someone to trigger scale and open a quick PR for audit.
Mike Patel: I’ll open the PR and request a fast review from @Sara. @ops-bot can you scale pool-east-2 +50%?
ops-bot: Scaling request accepted. pool-east-2: desired=8 -> 12 GPU nodes. Scaling job queued.
Mike Patel: PR opened: https://git.internal/routing/PR-482 — title: 'Canary fallback for ArgosHealth on pool-east-2' — reviewers: @Sara.
Ravi Kumar: Applying canary now (08:43Z). Command: ```curl -XPOST https://routing.internal/shift -d '{"customer":"argoshealth","to":"open-7b-quant","weight":70}'```
Sara Gomez: Confirming fallback will cut per-token latency substantially. Watch for cache warmup errors in the first 2 minutes.
ops-bot: pool-east-2 scaling: nodes provisioning (3/4) — expected ready ~08:49Z.
Elaine Chen: Please post a short status I can share with RM/customer: what we did, immediate impact, and ETA for full remediation.
Ravi Kumar: Fallback active at 08:44Z — routing shifted ~70% to open-7b-quant. Observed p99 drop from ~1.2s -> ~220ms in the canary. Some 503s during warmup but overall success rate improved.
Mike Patel: Quick sanity: run this to watch metrics: ```kubectl logs -f svc-routing -n prod | grep argoshealth``` — looking at error spikes.
Linda Park: I told ArgosHealth support that a fallback is live and we’re scaling nodes; they asked for a follow-up postmortem and a cost estimate for extra capacity.
Sara Gomez: Action items set: (1) Postmortem draft (owner: Elaine), (2) profile model and recommend permanent capacity or quantization (owner: Ravi), (3) alert tuning and runbook updates (owner: Mike).
Elaine Chen: I’ll draft the postmortem and PR the customer-facing note. ETA for draft EOD today.
Ravi Kumar: I will run a quick model-profile job and share perf numbers + suggested node counts by noon.
Mike Patel: Pinged reviewers for PR-482. If no objections in 10m I’ll merge and promote routing change to full rollout.
ops-bot: pool-east-2 nodes: provisioning complete (12/12) — autoscaling now active.
Ravi Kumar: With nodes up, we can gradually shift back. Plan: 10% increments every 2m to original model while monitoring p99.
Linda Park: Customer updated: appreciative of speed but wants SLA remediation plan. I’ll keep them posted.
Elaine Chen: Good work — keep this thread updated with final rollback plan and follow-up items.
Mike Patel: noted. will update when PR merged and when the routing rollback is complete. :thumbsup:
